status: ADAPTIVE follow-up. The hypothesis was formed after seeing the sw28 result in the restricted-view round, so an extra adaptive-selection cost is charged on top of the usual strict cost.
hypothesis: A short 28-day view of the same data enters the ridge as a MEAN-REVERSION CONTRAST against the long-history bases. For a user on a temporary activity spike the recent 28 days overstate the long-run rate, and the ensemble is improved by subtracting that component.
why_the_negative_weight_is_not_a_disqual: Adding sw28 with a negative coefficient to a pool already containing w409c and decay spans the same subspace as adding the contrast 'long minus recent-28' with a positive coefficient. The sign reflects parameterisation. The admitted pool of 130 itself carries negative weights on 85_probe_w210a (-0.098) and 83_probe_cls300 (-0.070), so negative coefficients are not disqualifying in the final model. The STRATEGY prohibition concerns inverting a FAILED PUBLIC PROBE after the fact; no probe was submitted here and the sign was measured offline on 96 splits.
window_specificity_supports_the_mechanis: Window 14 gives only +6.2e-06 and window 409 is the long baseline itself. The effect is specific to a short-but-not-tiny recent window, which is what a mean-reversion correction should look like rather than a generic short-window artefact.
channel_restriction_separately_refuted: All six channel-restricted views produced NEGATIVE incremental gain. Only the time restriction worked, so this is not a generic 'restricted view helps' claim.

gate_construction.adaptive_cost_note: DOUBLE the usual 0.00004, charged because this round is explicitly adaptive to an observed result.

reading_key.admit_only_if: public score clears the strict+adaptive gate computed with the doubled adaptive cost
reading_key.if_it_fails: branch closed permanently, no re-parameterisation, no threshold relaxation, no second probe on the same signal
